items.title: 52060_Eddie Barefield oral history interview
items.q: So then after that I also played at the Savoy with Don Redman. We made records. We made a lot of records while I was in that band.

ctx.x: Yeah, that's right. But now -- because that was the classical sound. But guys like John Nesbit and Don Redman started this, adding the sixth and then everybody started doing it. And they started using more pieces. Then they started adding the ninth and all of that and the 13th and 11th and everything in the chords.

So then the boppers did that, started using the augmented 11th. So finally they were using the whole scale. And they still haven't finished yet but someone cut the whole thing off around the 1940's.
